name: record_hypothesis
arguments: {"statement": "R525 sits in the kinase active-site region, where its positively charged side chain helps hold ATP or the phosphate groups. Replacing it with glutamine removes that charge and weakens nucleotide binding, which lowers catalytic output.", "mechanism_class": "ligand_binding", "supports": ["E2", "E7", "E16", "E17", "E10"], "would_refute": "Ligand-bound experimental structures (5P9J, 3K54 and other ATP or inhibitor complexes) observe residue 525, but no bound ATP, ADP or inhibitor atom lies within contact distance (about 5 \u00c5) of its side chain. A refutation would also come from a mutant model that keeps the same ligand contacts as the reference.", "starting_rank": 1, "rank_rationale": "This is the only hypothesis with direct support on this residue: UniProt (E2) states the variant disturbs ATP-binding, and the active-site annotation (E7) and the ibrutinib-bound structure (E16) both place residue 525 in the ligand-bearing region. Still missing: G1 and G2, since no paper tests R525Q itself, and G4, since no mutant structure exists. The E2 claim is a curated text note, not a measured binding result."}

name: record_hypothesis
arguments: {"statement": "R525 lies in a helix (residues 524\u2013526) and is highly conserved. Gln cannot make the same intrahelical or buried contacts as Arg, so the change destabilises the kinase fold and lowers the amount of properly folded protein.", "mechanism_class": "stability_folding", "supports": ["E5", "E13", "E14", "E15", "E10", "E19"], "would_refute": "Experimental structures show the R525 side chain is solvent-exposed with no buried partner, no intrahelical salt bridge or hydrogen bond, and no packing contact with neighbouring helices. Stability predictions for R525Q would also need to be near neutral, and the mutant model would need to keep the helix geometry and pLDDT of the reference.", "starting_rank": 2, "rank_rationale": "Conservation (E13 at 0.967), EVE (E15) and popEVE (E14) all point to a sensitive position, and the helix annotation (E5) makes a fold effect plausible. These are sequence-based or general predictions, though, and none is a measured stability or \u0394\u0394G value for R525Q. arguments: {"statement": "R525 contacts a regulatory or partner segment outside the kinase catalytic core, possibly through the activation loop or the kinase-domain interface with the SH3, SH2, or PH-TH region.
